disagreement_rows.builder: A methods and standardisation study by a working group: a cross-sectional calibration that linearly scales the outcome of any amyloid PET analysis method or tracer onto a 0 to 100 'Centiloid' (CL) scale anchored at the mean of young controls (0) and the mean of typical Alzheimer's disease patients (100). The process has three levels: Level-1 defines the standard method and the anchor points; Level-2 is how an independent site calibrates its own tracer or method to the scale; Level-3 is exact reproduction of an already-calibrated method as a pipeline check.

Two anchor groups plus a separate VOI-definition set: cognitively normal subjects under 45 years of age (34 young controls, 31.5 ± 6.3 years, range 22-43); patients diagnosed with AD by 1984 NINCDS-ADRDA criteria with a Clinical Dementia Rating global score of 0.5 or 1 (45 analysed, mean age 67.5 ± 10.5 yrs, range 50 to 89); and separately 19 AD-CTX subjects and 25 amyloid-negative older controls used only to define the cortical target region
disagreement_rows.critic: young controls (≤45 years) and typical Alzheimer’s disease patients

all_rows.builder: The 'standard PiB method' — PiB 50-70 min SUVr computed with the standard CTX target VOI and whole cerebellum (WC) reference VOI — is the reference against which any non-standard method or other tracer is calibrated; an F-18 tracer already directly calibrated to it may serve as a surrogate reference, no more than one step removed from PiB

[C-11]Pittsburgh Compound-B (PiB) PET, 10-15 mCi injected, with the standard measure taken as the 50-70 min post-injection SUVr; FDG PET (~7 mCi) was additionally acquired in 13 AD-CTX subjects to build the cerebellar gray reference region

none stated — the paper describes no adjustment for multiple comparisons; its quality criteria are correlation-based acceptance thresholds (slope, intercept, R 2) and a relative variance ratio rather than hypothesis tests
